observed_result.verdict_scope: criterion = comparable fresh G02 measurements for all three candidates with one methodology on this machine, and the distributable artifacts run in clean environments without each candidate's toolchain. Windows artifacts were inspected statically only (native execution blocked). This is not a product-requirement verdict and not a selection of a candidate.

methodology.interleaving: round-robin over go, rust, ts and a no-op control; the starting member rotates every iteration; 2 independent passes (A then B) at different times
methodology.startup: subprocess spawn to exit wall time (perf_counter), stdout captured and checked after timing; 10 warmups then 100 samples per candidate per pass (200 pooled); control = /usr/bin/true
methodology.rss: /usr/bin/time -l, maximum resident set size (bytes, macOS) and peak memory footprint; 15 runs per candidate per pass after 1-2 warmups (30 pooled); TUI RSS covers first frame, 20 x j, '/' + 'host-05', Esc, q on large-100
methodology.tui_first_frame: launch (before Popen) until the pyte screen shows every alias and the N/M status (homelab 3/3; large-100 first 10 aliases and 100/100); arrival time of the chunk after which the predicate became true, pyte parse time excluded; 30 per pass; control = /usr/bin/printf through the same pty path
methodology.tui_keystroke: write of one key to chunk arrival that makes the expected screen state true: j moves selection to expected alias, filter characters make status line show typed text and expected N/100, Esc restores 100/100; 30 sessions per pass x (20 j + 7 filter chars + Esc); also time to first output byte
methodology.tui_idle: user+sys CPU from /usr/bin/time -l of a TUI held idle 30 s after first frame minus a 2 s hold, 2 runs per candidate per pass; time -l resolution is 10 ms so this is a coarse estimate (unchanged from round 1). Round 2 adds idle_long: 300 s holds, 3 reps per candidate, interleaved (see idle_long_hold_300s)
methodology.cold_first_exec: fresh copy of dist/darwin-arm64 to /tmp, version --json executed 3 times in a row (first execution of a freshly written file vs next two); not a reboot-cold measurement
methodology.env: PATH=/usr/bin:/bin, HOME/TMPDIR/cwd in a private /tmp sandbox, TERM=xterm-256color for TUI, no SSH_AUTH_SOCK; pty 80x24

observed_result.round2_scope: Round 2 re-measures all three darwin-arm64 artifacts in one session with the round-1 methodology (same scripts, same arguments) because the go and rust artifacts changed after round 1 (sha256 differs); ts artifacts are byte-identical to round 1 (see artifact_sha256_same_as_round1). Clean-environment darwin/linux runs were repeated for go and rust only; ts clean runs are reused from round 1 (clean_environment_runs.reused_from_round1). Windows static inspection was re-run for all three (cheap, static).

idle_long_hold_300s.method: idle_long.py: 3 reps x 3 candidates, each rep visits the candidates round-robin with the start member rotated; per visit one 300 s idle hold after the first large-100 frame and one 2 s short hold, both under /usr/bin/time -l; gross = idle cpu / idle real, net = (idle cpu - mean short cpu) / (idle real - mean short real)

observed_result.spec_15_1_context: First useful TUI frame P95 <= 750 ms, key handling P95 <= 100 ms, idle RSS <= 150 MiB, idle CPU < 0.5% of a core (5-minute sample). These slice numbers cover a trivial local profile viewer, not the product, and do not settle those budgets.

limitations: Single machine (Apple M5 Max, 18 cores, macOS 27.0) shared with other agent workloads. Round-2 1-minute load average was about 6-7 of 18 cores at the start of pass 1 and about 1.5-2.6 for most of pass 2 and the idle hold (see environment.load_per_pass and idle_long_hold_300s.load); round 1 ran at about 4-10. The load differed between rounds and between passes, so small round-to-round differences (a few percent) are within what this noise can produce; no attempt was made to isolate the machine. Numbers are comparable between candidates and rounds here, not portable to other hardware.

Latencies come from Python spawn plus a pyte terminal emulator, not a real terminal: a floor of about 2.2 ms (spawn) and 4.0-4.3 ms (pty path) is included, shown by the control rows. pyte answers only DA/DSR queries; a real terminal answers more capability queries, which could change the ts first-frame time.

Keystroke latency excludes pyte parse time but includes pty and scheduler delay. The go filter-typing P95 of about 16 ms is consistent with a 60 fps renderer tick; that explanation is an inference and was not isolated.

RSS uses /usr/bin/time -l (macOS rusage max RSS, bytes). It is not comparable to Windows working set or Linux RSS. Idle memory over time was not measured separately (the idle holds report max RSS of a process that also ran first frame).

Idle CPU: the 300 s hold (3 reps per candidate, interleaved) is the spec 15.1 style 5-minute sample for the large-100 profile viewer only, on darwin-arm64, via /usr/bin/time -l (10 ms CPU resolution); it excludes the 2 s startup+first-frame CPU by subtracting a 2 s hold. It says nothing about a product TUI with a live agent connection, host probing, or file watching. The 30 s estimate in the main run is kept for round-1 comparability and is coarser.
Cold-start in the spec sense (after reboot or purged page cache) was not measured; the cold_first_exec rows only compare the first run of a freshly copied file with later runs.

linux-x64 ran emulated (linux/amd64 on an arm64 Docker Desktop VM; /proc/cpuinfo showed VirtualApple in round 1, which suggests Rosetta, an inference); it proves loading and behavior, not native x86-64 speed or behavior. Linux timings in the records are incidental, not benchmarks.

Linux binaries were copied into containers with docker cp and run as root with --network none; the shared fake-agent socket used a docker volume. The TUI check ran through docker exec -it in a host pty.

Native Windows execution blocked: no Windows host. Windows artifacts were inspected for file type, size, sha256 and PE headers only. Nothing about Windows named-pipe, console, or signal behavior is established.

macOS: artifacts are ad-hoc signed only (not notarized); Gatekeeper/quarantine behavior for downloaded files was not tested. The writes check lists files in fresh TMPDIR/HOME/cwd only; writes elsewhere were not traced (no fs_usage/dtruss without privileges). Linux docker diff covers the whole container filesystem except mounted volumes.

ts clean-environment runs (darwin, linux-arm64, linux-x64, musl probe) are reused from round 1, not re-run: the ts artifacts have identical sha256 to round 1 (artifact_sha256_same_as_round1). The ts timing rows were re-measured in round 2. The fake-agent contact counts for the round-2 darwin/linux clean runs cover go and rust only (4 connections each); the darwin note text inside clean-darwin.json still says 6 because it is a fixed string in clean_env.py.

Conformance status is not judged here. The task packet states round-2 conformance: go 133p/0f/0e darwin and linux, rust 133p/0f/0e darwin and linux, ts darwin 126p/7f/0e and linux 127p/6f/0e; this record does not re-verify those counts, and ts timing rows were measured on a candidate that fails some conformance checks.
Prototype REPORT.md numbers were not reused; all numbers here were measured fresh, from prototypes/*/dist as found (never rebuilt by this task).

round3.scope: go and rust darwin-arm64 only, re-measured with the round-2 scripts and arguments after rounds 3b/3c changed their run/TUI code. ts is frozen and was not re-measured: its rows stay in the round-2 content of this file. Artifacts are prototypes/{go,rust}/dist as found (not rebuilt), sha256 verified against dist/manifest.json before the run (artifact_inventory_pre) and unchanged after it. The only script change: g02bench.CANDIDATES honours HM_G02_CANDS (candidate subset); no method change. Because the subset has 2 candidates + control instead of 3 + control, the round-robin neighbours differ from round 2.

harness_floors_control_rows.note: keystroke latency has no control row in measure.py (round 2 and 3 alike); the pty-path floor is the control first-frame row (control printf through the same pty path)

idle_long_hold_300s.method: idle_long.py unchanged from round 2 (HM_G02_CANDS=go,rust): 3 reps x 2 candidates, round-robin, start member rotated per rep; per visit one 300 s idle hold after the first large-100 frame and one 2 s short hold under /usr/bin/time -l; gross = idle cpu / idle real; net = (idle cpu - mean short cpu) / (idle real - mean short real)

limitations: Single machine (Apple M5 Max, 18 cores) shared with other workloads; no isolation was attempted. At the start the 1-minute load average was about 3.0-3.3 (background: a dev app near 25% of one core and a speech-to-text process near 22% of one core, which was still running at the start; nothing build- or test-heavy was running, so the run was not delayed). Load stayed about 1.5-5.1 through the run (load_summary, environment.load_per_pass). Round 2 ran at about 1.5-7. Numbers are comparable between candidates in this run; round-to-round differences of a few percent are within what this noise can produce.

The pty control floor moved between rounds: control first-frame p50 was 4.3 / 4.0 ms (homelab / large-100) in round 2 and 6.3 / 5.7 ms in round 3, and the /usr/bin/true spawn floor was 2.26 ms in round 2 and 2.10 ms in round 3. The rust first-frame rise (+24% / +8.5% raw p50) is of the same size as the pty floor shift; the p50_minus_control_p50_ms rows show rust at 0.9 / 4.6 ms above the floor in round 3 versus 1.4 / 5.5 ms in round 2. Whether the pty floor shift is machine state or a measurement artifact of the 2-candidate rotation was not isolated.

Because the candidate set is go, rust and control (3 members) instead of go, rust, ts and control (4 members), the round-robin neighbours and cache pressure differ from round 2; the method is otherwise unchanged (same scripts, same arguments, g02bench.CANDIDATES now honours HM_G02_CANDS).

Latencies come from Python spawn plus a pyte terminal emulator, not a real terminal; the control rows show the spawn and pty floors. Keystroke latency has no control row. The go filter-typing p95 (about 16 ms) matches a 60 fps renderer tick; that explanation is an inference from round 2 and was not isolated. K17 (filter p95 <= 100 ms) is read here as the filter_type_ms p95 of this method (420 filter keystrokes per candidate: 60 sessions x 7 characters); this record is not a gate verdict.
RSS is /usr/bin/time -l maximum resident set size (macOS bytes); not comparable to Windows working set or Linux RSS. The 300 s idle hold report max RSS of a process that also ran first frame.

Idle CPU is a 300 s hold, 3 reps per candidate, via /usr/bin/time -l (10 ms CPU resolution), large-100 viewer only, darwin-arm64; it is not a product TUI with live connections. The 30 s per-pass estimate in per_pass_drift is coarse and kept for comparability only.

go idle CPU (0.35% of one core, 1.04-1.06 s CPU per 300 s, roughly half user and half sys) is nonzero and not 0.0x%; round 2 gave 0.34%. Spec 15.1 target is < 0.5%: go sits at about 70% of that margin. The cause (a periodic tick versus other work) was not investigated here.
Cold-first-exec rows compare the first execution of a freshly copied file with later ones (per_pass_drift); not a reboot-cold measurement.

Only darwin-arm64 binaries were executed. linux and windows artifacts were hashed and sized only (sha256 verified against dist/manifest.json); no clean-environment, conformance, or Windows/Linux timing runs were part of this task. Windows artifacts were never run (blocked: no Windows host).

Artifact sizes: exe bytes are raw; gzip9_exe_bytes is `gzip -9 -n` of the file; tar_gz9_bytes is the round-2 method (tar of the artifact directory, gzip level 9, mtime 0). All eight go/rust artifact sha256 differ from round 2 (rebuilt after rounds 3b/3c); sizes changed by 0-0.9%.
Conformance status is not judged here; ts rows remain the frozen round-2 ones in the round-2 content of this file.
